title: refactor(driver-sql): move the autonumber sequence path out of sql-driver.ts into sql-driver-autonumber.ts (#25521 cut 11)

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XXYaoUKRhjtA4WcF7E86RCH)_

Ruling-ref: 6270097840

Cut 11 of the `sql-driver.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). The claim is `6424911800`. The cut opens with a fresh seam table (below), taken on `origin/main` after cut 10 merged, and takes the area that pays best without breaking a series limit. The bodies of six `SqlDriver` methods move unedited into a new seam module, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-autonumber.ts`, through a new host, `AutonumberHost`. Together they are the autonumber sequence path:

- `getNextSequenceValue`, which reads and advances one counter row under its lock (and bootstraps a cold counter from the data);
- `fillAutoNumberFields`, which fills a row's `autonumber` fields from those counters;
- `issueAutonumbers` (public), the issue-ahead door, with its collision follow-up;
- `maxAutonumberCounter`, the bootstrap reading of the highest counter in a set of values;
- `collidingAutoNumberReservations` and `resyncSequenceToDataMax`, the #5495 collision re-seed.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for later cuts. There is no `docs/adr/**` edit, no `packages/spec/**` edit, no anchor entry change and no new gate. Branch `claude/project-thread-r8r6to` (the platform assigned it to this card thread, as the claim records). One commit, `69181bf14`, on `origin/main` `817cb8983` (cut 10's merge).

**Net line count (the seat's rule).** `sql-driver.ts` goes from 21,018 lines to 20,827: **-191**.

- Out: the six bodies, 248 lines (79 + 61 + 51 + 21 + 11 + 25), and the two import lines of `isUniqueViolationError` and `uniqueViolationColumn`, whose last reader moved. Three more such names (`renderAutonumber`, `readAutonumberCounter`, `missingFieldValues`) leave a line that stays.
- In: the six stub bodies, 54 lines (13 + 9 + 11 + 2 + 7 + 12, each 4 + 2 per field read + 1 per method read; `maxAutonumberCounter` reads no member, so its stub is a comment and a direct call), and 5 lines for the new import and its comment.
- Priced before the move at -194 for the bodies alone.
- The new module is 367 lines.

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** I read the full file list of every open PR at start (36 PRs, on cut 10's head) and again after cut 10 merged, before the first edit (28 PRs). No open PR touches `sql-driver.ts`, `turso-driver.ts`, the CRUD section, `check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` or the driver-sql anchor entries.

- #26261 (`$now` comparand) was open at start, editing the preamble and Filter helpers. It merged before cut 10 did, so it is in this base.
- #26138 touches `driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts` only, and #26267 the `vitest.config.ts` of driver-turso and driver-sqlite-wasm only.
- `origin/main` has moved 8 commits past the base since; none touches `packages/drivers/**`.

### Pricing the eligible methods

A method is eligible to move when its return type is annotated or it is not public; it has no `getBuilder` site, no `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site, no private or protected static read, no `super` read, no bare `this` pass and no write to `this`; and it is not `insertOnlyUpsertColumns`. 164 members are eligible on this base. Each is priced as its stub minus its body (a stub costs 4 lines, plus 2 per field or getter read and 1 per method read).

**Priced by area** (every eligible body with a negative price and no `sql-driver.ts#…` pointer, summed per section): Filter helpers -550 (22 bodies), Rotation -388 (15), CRUD -351 (18), and every other section -93 or less.

The highest-priced candidates, and why each one stays or moves:

## Why this area

- **It pays the most of any area that moves cleanly.** Filter helpers' paying bodies each drag module-local refusal helpers that other members also read; under the series' helper rule (a body that drags a shared helper stays) what is left there pays about -100. Rotation's paying bodies read eight shared module-local declarations, as cut 10 measured. In CRUD, the sequence path is the part that moves with one shared declaration.
- **One shared declaration, exported in place (cut 2's shape).** `SEQUENCES_TABLE` is read by the two moved bodies and by three members that stay: `ensureSequencesTable`, `ensureSequencesKeyHashShape` and the `sequencesTableName` getter. It stays in `sql-driver.ts`, gains `export`, and the module imports it back, as cut 2 did with seven declarations. The value import is read only inside function bodies, so the module cycle is evaluation-safe. `index.ts` does not re-export it, and the published `.d.ts` does not move (proof below).
- **What stays, and why.**
  - `ensureSequencesTable` and `ensureSequencesKeyHashShape` write `this`.
  - `autoNumberValueExists` and `scanMaxNumericTail` each hold one of the four tenant-column predicates that `check:tenant-chokepoint`'s ADR-0131 D8 rule recognises. That gate scans the three driver files, not seam modules, and does not print the count on success, so moving them would narrow it silently (its floor is 3). I measured the count with the gate's own `nullArmsOf`: **4 at base and 4 at head**, all four in `sql-driver.ts`.
  - The sequence-semantics members `TursoDriver`'s remote face calls (`resolveSequenceTenantId`, `sequenceKeyHash`, `defineSequencesTable`, `createSequencesTable` and two getters) and the generic `attemptWithoutPoisoning` price at -3 or better, so they stay.
- **No series limit is touched:** none of the six builds through `getBuilder`, reads a static, has a `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site, uses `super` or a bare `this`, or writes to `this`. `issueAutonumbers`, the one public method, has an annotated return type (a promise of `string[][]`).
- **Subclasses.** `TursoDriver` overrides `getNextSequenceValue`, `autoNumberValueExists` and `resyncSequenceToDataMax`, and each override calls `super` on its local path. The stubs stay on the class with the same signatures, so `super` still reaches them. The moved bodies reach every method through a late-bound closure on the instance, so `fillAutoNumberFields` still reaches Turso's counter, and the collision path still reaches its `autoNumberValueExists` and `resyncSequenceToDataMax`.
- **Path readers, screened.** No script, test, doc or ADR names any of the six by a `sql-driver.ts#…` path or a `sql-driver.ts::…` key. No test slices their text out of `sql-driver.ts`. See Acceptance notes for prose that names them.

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1-10 apply it)

- Each class method keeps its docblock and signature, byte-identical less `async`. Its body is now one host literal plus `NAME.call(host, ...)`, marked `[#25521 cut 11]`. The five `async` methods return the moved function's own promise. `maxAutonumberCounter` reads no member, so its stub calls the function directly, as cut 3/16 of #25467 did.
- Fields go as GETTERS that read the driver at call time: `autoNumberFields`, `issuedAutoNumbers`, `knex`, `physicalTableByObject` and `sequencesHasKeyHash`. Methods go as closures that call the method on the driver at call time. So a subclass override, an instance spy, or a field replaced after construction is still the one the body reaches (see the probe below).
- Each moved function types its `this` as the Pick of `AutonumberHost` over exactly the members it reads. Each stub annotates its literal as the ThisParameterType of the moved function. There is no cast, and no member becomes public.
- `AutonumberHost` lists 17 members, each typed as the class member's indexed access.
- **Module-level declarations.** The module imports `DriverOptions` (type), `missingFieldValues`, `readAutonumberCounter` and `renderAutonumber` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, `StorageNameMapping` from `@objectstack/spec/system`, `isUniqueViolationError` and `uniqueViolationColumn` from `@objectstack/types`, the type `Knex`, `GLOBAL_TENANT` from `schema-drift.ts`, the types `AutoNumberReservation` and `SqlDriver`, and `SEQUENCES_TABLE` from `sql-driver.ts`. `sql-driver.ts` drops the five of those names it no longer reads.
- **Comments.** The module header says what moved, what stayed and why, and how the bodies reach the class. The module has no anchor entry, so the header's own mention of the ADR-0131 D8 rule counts nowhere. The `sql-driver.ts` import comment names cut 11 in 4 lines.
- **How the move was made.** A script produced it from the source text; nothing was retyped. Each body line is re-indented two columns. No line in the moved bodies starts inside template-literal text.

## ADR anchors

`check:adr-anchors` counts decision-letter citations on the anchored surface: each anchor's `invariant`, plus the full text of each anchored file.

- **The count.** It is **1880 at base `817cb8983` and 1879 at head `69181bf14`**, over 90 anchored files at both ends. Both runs exit 0.
- **Why it drops by one.** `getNextSequenceValue`'s body carries one comment that cites `ADR-0131 D9` (the organization-less counter refusal happens first). That comment moves from the anchored `sql-driver.ts` to the new module, which has no anchor entry. The refusal itself (`resolveSequenceTenantId`) stays in `sql-driver.ts`.
- **No entry needs a new home.** The only `sql-driver.ts` entry is ADR-0053's, whose paragraph describes `formatOutput` and `presentReadValue`; neither moved. No new entry was added, and no `scripts/adr-anchors/**` file changed.

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

This is measured under the series bar (ruling `6348891160`, item 1).

- **How each end was built.** `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/driver-sql --force` at each end, against the same dependency tree. The base leg writes base `sql-driver.ts` into this worktree and removes the new module after the commit, under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that restores HEAD. The restore is proved by the HEAD blob hashes (`13a5215f`, `026dfdda`), an empty `git diff HEAD` and 0 status entries.
- **The hashes.** The raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` is the same at base and at head: `0f33bf3febaac3c7aa96f68a4226d752766b8203ab7acade523b69f9aaa44d74`. `cmp` finds them identical.
- **Positive control.** I dropped `protected` from `getNextSequenceValue` in the head `index.d.ts`. The result hashes to `bbd6f18ba89c1fdbfa84c1bb16628d3e6956f8c4b2c8296d7629f75e63de20cb`, with a 1-line diff and `cmp` exit 1.
- **Export lists.** CJS `require` and ESM `import` of the built dist give 59 / 59 names at both ends, identical (`SEQUENCES_TABLE` is not among them).
- **The head dist carries the move.** `.call(host` sites in `index.mjs` go from 30 at base to 35 at head (five; `maxAutonumberCounter` is a direct call).

The four that differ: the `@objectstack/spec/data` and `@objectstack/types` imports (names dropped), `SEQUENCES_TABLE` (a leading `export`, nothing else) and the class. The one new statement is the import of the new module.

- **Negative control.** I changed `legacy shape. ` to `legacy shap3. ` in a module copy. The proof then reports `getNextSequenceValue` with its body tokens and lines differing, prints `PROOF FAILED`, and exits 1.

## Tests

Each end ran under one `os-verify-lock` hold, after building that end's driver-sql dist. I compared the vitest JSON per test name and status, base `817cb8983` against head `69181bf14`. Every part's exit code was captured on its own (build, probe, three suites: all 0 at both ends).

| `@objectstack/driver-turso`, against that end's built driver-sql dist | 2526 (2492 passed, 34 skipped; 95 files) | same | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` | 746 (746 passed; 39 files) | same | 0 / 0 / 0 |

- **Type check and lint.** `tsc --noEmit -p .` in driver-sql exits 0. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config packages/drivers/driver-sql` exits 0, with 0 problems.
- **Late-binding probe.** A scratch script, not committed. It runs node against each end's built dist on in-memory SQLite. Its 33 readings print identical output at base and head (`diff` is empty). They cover:
  1. `create` reaching a SUBCLASS override of `getNextSequenceValue` through `fillAutoNumberFields`, with the arguments it passes;
  2. `getNextSequenceValue` reaching instance spies on `ensureSequencesTable`, `resolveSequenceTenantId`, `sequenceKeyHash`, `scanMaxNumericTail` and `attemptWithoutPoisoning`, cold and warm;
  3. `sequencesHasKeyHash` flipped on the instance: a scoped format answers the legacy-shape refusal;
  4. `fillAutoNumberFields` reading `physicalTableByObject` and `autoNumberFields` replaced after construction (the scan then names the replaced table; an emptied registry fills nothing), through an instance spy on `getNextSequenceValue`;
  5. `issueAutonumbers` ahead of a write and after a collision (a column-named one and a column-blind one), through instance spies on `injectTenantOnInsert`, `fillAutoNumberFields`, `collidingAutoNumberReservations`, `autoNumberValueExists`, `autoNumberCounterKey` and `resyncSequenceToDataMax`; the transaction early-out; and `issuedAutoNumbers` replaced after construction;
  6. the #5495 re-seed through `create`, reaching instance overrides of `autoNumberValueExists` and `resyncSequenceToDataMax`;
  7. `maxAutonumberCounter` on three value sets;
  8. bad arguments: each async method answers a rejection, and `maxAutonumberCounter` throws synchronously, at both ends (it was never `async`).
- **Not run.** No ablation, because no tested behaviour changed. `test:repo` was not run locally: the diff touches no repo-project test, and CI's Test Core runs it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Prose that names a moved body by file.** ADR-0034 says `getNextSequenceValue` "uses `runner = parentTrx ?? this.knex` … (`sql-driver.ts`)". The method still lives on `SqlDriver` in that file; its body now runs from `sql-driver-autonumber.ts`. Left as is: no `docs/adr/**` edit in this series.
- **One comment now points at an import that left.** The comment on `isUnbackedConflictTargetError` in `sql-driver.ts` (line 2196) warns "Deliberately NOT `isUniqueViolationError`, which is imported one line away". `sql-driver.ts` no longer imports that predicate (its last reader moved). The warning stays true; "imported one line away" no longer does. Left unedited because the cut is move-only.
- `TursoDriver`'s docblocks name `SqlDriver.getNextSequenceValue`, `SqlDriver.maxAutonumberCounter` and the others as the members its remote face shares; each is still a member of `SqlDriver`.
- **Next slice, priced on this base.** The remaining CRUD upsert code needs the five conflict-target declarations (cut 2's export shape would cover them). Filter helpers stays the largest area, but its paying bodies share refusal helpers with the members that stay.
